Assign area by the component/field that must be fixed — nodeSelector, affinity, tolerations, readiness gates to scheduling; kubelet behavior, terminating PVCs, projected token volumes to node or storage; Service connectivity to network — not by the workload object (Pod, Deployment, Job) or surface symptom where it appears.
Reports phrased as why, whether, is-supported, how-to, or meaning/consultation questions without reproduction steps, identified defect, or concrete proposal are support, not bug or feature.

rules.text: Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.
Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.

Kind is bug only when the report shows incorrect behaviour of existing functionality plus concrete defect evidence such as reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace; symptom-only or environment-triggered reports without such evidence are support.

Issues about stuck resources, feature-gates having no effect, proxy/NO_PROXY/CIDR handling, upgrade/migration help, or how to monitor/observe behavior without clear evidence of a code defect are support, not bug; a specific kubectl flag being ignored with reproducible steps is bug.

Issues about KMS/KMSv2, encryption at rest, DEK, and certificates belong to area auth, and issues about DRA, ResourceSlice, ResourceClaim, and device allocation belong to area node, regardless of generic terms like cache, validation, or scheduling.
Improvements to error messages, validation messages, or existing test coverage for existing functionality are kind bug, not feature.

An indefinite retry loop or concrete data-plane failure naming the operation and observed wrong result counts as defect evidence for bug and is not stuck-resource support, while privilege-escalation claims, admission wildcard questions, or validation rejections without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support.

Reports of unable-to-authenticate or certificate-signing failures, fake-client or test-helper unexpected results, kubectl patch having no effect, or bare resource-name titles without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support, not bug.

If auth or apps keywords such as token, service-account, RBAC, or controller co-occur with infrastructure signals such as kubelet, PVC/volume terminating state, readiness gates, endpoints, or scheduler behavior, choose the infrastructure area node, storage, network, or scheduling over auth or apps.

Issues invoking port-forward including socat errors belong to area network, and issues about kubectl annotate or annotation handling belong to area cli, regardless of mentioning kubectl or generic API terms.

Even with reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace, reports about missing API fields/labels/permissions, missing retry or handling for edge/race/recreate cases, inability to combine auth options, data races, silent-ignore or potential-incorrect logic, or wrong HTTP/status return values requiring behavior change are kind feature, not bug.

Reports mentioning CoreDNS/coredns/DNS timeout logs without reproduction steps are support in area apps, not network, and reports about ineffective RBAC role resource-name restrictions/validation are bug in area api-machinery, not support/auth.

rules.text: Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.
Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.

Kind is bug only with clear reproduction/evidence of broken existing functionality; how-to/usage questions, stuck resources without reproduction, config/plugin/migration confusion, or missing-flag parity requests are support or feature, not bug.
Looping behavior, post-restart degradation, or output formatting differences without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or logs proving broken existing functionality are support, not bug.
Missing API validation, acceptance of invalid or empty objects, incorrect field immutability, and panics on invalid input are bug, not feature, even when phrased as a make/allow request.

Reports of incorrect documentation for existing flags, misleading or unnecessarily scary events/messages, or unexpected controller/CSI operations with logs or observed behavior are bug, not feature or support, even when phrased as a change request or Why/usage question.

High-churn OOM/resource exhaustion or stale node status/metrics after external changes like disk expansion without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs is support/feature, not bug, while terminating pods still appearing in endpoints/services with observed behavior and version info is bug, not support.

Scheduling queue, preemption/priority and custom scheduling policy belong to area scheduling (not apps), while CronJob/Job schedule expressions, timing misses and how-to cron usage questions belong to area apps, and service IP block refresh / API-server Get "https://" connectivity failures belong to area api-machinery (not network).

DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation, resource claims/pools, AllocationMode, conversion/fuzz helpers) belongs to area node (not scheduling or api-machinery), and dynamic admission webhook resource matching for subresources like pods/exec, pods/attach and portforward belongs to area api-machinery (not auth) and is support without crash/panic or logs proving broken existing functionality.

HostPath/device (/dev/*) mount open permission denials despite capabilities are bug in area storage (not support/node), and clock-skew/time-drift induced ServiceAccount token invalid states are support in area node (not bug/auth).

Race-condition memory leaks with identified component/code location and persistent memory growth after deletion are bug even without minimal reproducer, while documentation ordering/versioning questions and fake-client/test-harness behavior differences without crash/panic are support, not bug.

Kubelet serving CSR / certificate issuance failures and extension-apiserver-authentication configmap write conflicts belong to area auth (not node or api-machinery), and with observed upgrade behavior or logs are bug, not support.

Missing retry logic, missing RBAC resource coverage, missing metric labels, unsupported auth-combination limits, potential/unproven logic flaws, transient coexistence on rapid delete/recreate, and suboptimal controller return values or HTTP status codes without crash/panic or proven broken user workflow are feature, not bug.

Reports phrased as Can't/Cannot create/view, Restrict by/to, or Failed to make request / version-conversion errors about existing kubectl CLI behavior, scheduling placement constraints, or webhook authenticator version handling without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs are support, not bug or feature.
Kubeconfig usage/conf questions and apiserver failed-calling-webhook or AdmissionReview version-conversion errors belong to area auth (not api-machinery).

Questions about client-go, Clientset, informers, watch, or calling exec/shell via Go API belong to area api-machinery (not cli), and informer/watch panic reports without stack trace, logs, or minimal reproducer are support, not bug.

High-churn OOM/resource exhaustion or stale node status/metrics after external changes like disk expansion without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs is support/feature, not bug, while terminating pods still appearing in endpoints/services with observed behavior and version info is bug, not support.

DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation, resource claims/pools, AllocationMode, conversion/fuzz helpers) belongs to area node (not scheduling or api-machinery), and dynamic admission webhook resource matching for subresources like pods/exec, pods/attach and portforward belongs to area api-machinery (not auth) and is support without crash/panic or logs proving broken existing functionality.

HostPath/device (/dev/*) mount open permission denials despite capabilities are bug in area storage (not support/node), and clock-skew/time-drift induced ServiceAccount token invalid states are support in area node (not bug/auth).

Missing retry logic, missing RBAC resource coverage, missing metric labels, unsupported auth-combination limits, potential/unproven logic flaws, transient coexistence on rapid delete/recreate, and suboptimal controller return values or HTTP status codes without crash/panic or proven broken user workflow are feature, not bug.

Reports phrased as Can't/Cannot create/view, Restrict by/to, or Failed to make request / version-conversion errors about existing kubectl CLI behavior, scheduling placement constraints, or webhook authenticator version handling without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs are support, not bug or feature.

Kind is bug only when the report shows incorrect behaviour of existing functionality plus concrete defect evidence such as reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace; symptom-only or environment-triggered reports without such evidence are support.

Issues about stuck resources, feature-gates having no effect, proxy/NO_PROXY/CIDR handling, upgrade/migration help, or how to monitor/observe behavior without clear evidence of a code defect are support, not bug; a specific kubectl flag being ignored with reproducible steps is bug.

Missing retry logic, missing RBAC resource coverage, missing metric labels, unsupported auth-combination limits, potential/unproven logic flaws, transient coexistence on rapid delete/recreate, and suboptimal controller return values or HTTP status codes without crash/panic or proven broken user workflow are feature, not bug.

Reports phrased as Can't/Cannot create/view, Restrict by/to, or Failed to make request / version-conversion errors about existing kubectl CLI behavior, scheduling placement constraints, or webhook authenticator version handling without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs are support, not bug or feature.
Kubeconfig usage/conf questions and apiserver failed-calling-webhook or AdmissionReview version-conversion errors belong to area auth (not api-machinery).

Questions about client-go, Clientset, informers, watch, or calling exec/shell via Go API belong to area api-machinery (not cli), and informer/watch panic reports without stack trace, logs, or minimal reproducer are support, not bug.

Reports that secrets encryption is 'not working' or securityContext runAsUser/runAsGroup values 'don't reflect' inside containers without a minimal reproducer plus config/logs proving broken existing functionality are support, not bug.

Scheduler failure-to-schedule/unschedulable due to topologySpreadConstraints, PVCs, or DRA consumable capacity/counters/allocationMode, kube-scheduler panics, and scheduler-perf test failures with described observed behavior belong to area scheduling and are bug, not support, even without minimal reproducer.

PVC/PV binding phase mismatches (PV bound but PVC pending) and volume-expansion node status (NodeResizePending) persisting after successful operation with described observed behavior are bug in area storage, not support, even without a minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs.

EgressSelectorConfiguration (including TLS Server Name overrides) and kube-apiserver upgrade deadlocks involving admission webhooks and default egress belong to area api-machinery (not network or auth).

Incorrect Pod phase/status display (Completed vs Error, OutOfcpu) and missing expected auto-populated fields (e.g., service-account secrets field empty) with described observed behavior are bug, not support, even without minimal reproducer, and Deployment placement on master/control-plane nodes and OutOfcpu status belong to area apps/node/cli as appropriate, not scheduling.

Concurrent-map panics on pod creation with empty volumes, severe Local PV copy slowdown after node reboot resolved by recreation, and garbage-collector deletion of StatefulSet dependents on repeated recreation with described observed behavior are bug in area storage for volume cases and apps for StatefulSet GC (not node/api-machinery/support/feature), even without minimal reproducer.

Controller failure to enqueue/reconcile all affected objects on relevant events, truncated init-container/workload execution after node restart, and insecure default volume permissions (e.g., 777 for ConfigMap/Secret volumes) with described observed behavior are bug, not support/feature, even without minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or logs and even when phrased as consider/question.

FsGroupPolicy to access-mode coverage gaps (e.g., policy not applying to new access mode) and incorrect volume/PVC capacity bytes from stats/summary or volume metrics with described observed behavior are bug in area storage (not node/support/feature), even without minimal reproducer, crash/panic, or regression logs.

Reports explicitly invoking kubectl (create -f, apply, run) including permission failures for normal users, last-applied-configuration/replica-count drift, and run/workload placement after untainting master/control-plane nodes belong to area cli (not auth/node/apps).
Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.
Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.
If a report describes incorrect behaviour of existing functionality, kind is bug.
Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.
Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.

Kind is bug only when the report shows incorrect behaviour of existing functionality plus concrete defect evidence such as reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace; question-form or configure/how-to reports and does-not-respect or invalid-value reports without such evidence are support, not bug or feature, except a named memory leak with component counts as defect evidence for bug.

Issues about stuck resources, feature-gates having no effect, proxy/NO_PROXY/CIDR handling, upgrade/migration help, or how to monitor/observe behavior without clear evidence of a code defect are support, not bug; a specific kubectl flag being ignored with reproducible steps is bug.

Issues about KMS/KMSv2, encryption at rest, DEK, and certificates belong to area auth, and issues about DRA, ResourceSlice, ResourceClaim, and device allocation belong to area node, unless they describe scheduler behavior such as SharedCounters, binding, queueing, or scheduling decisions, which belong to area scheduling.
Improvements to error messages, validation messages, or existing test coverage for existing functionality are kind bug, not feature.

An indefinite retry loop or concrete data-plane failure naming the operation and observed wrong result counts as defect evidence for bug and is not stuck-resource support, while privilege-escalation claims, admission wildcard questions, or validation rejections without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support.

Reports of unable-to-authenticate or certificate-signing failures, fake-client or test-helper unexpected results, kubectl patch having no effect, or bare resource-name titles without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support, not bug.

If auth or apps keywords such as token, service-account, RBAC, or controller co-occur with infrastructure signals such as kubelet, PVC/volume terminating state, readiness gates, endpoints, or scheduler behavior, choose the infrastructure area node, storage, network, or scheduling over auth or apps.

Issues invoking port-forward including socat errors belong to area network, and issues about kubectl annotate or annotation handling or kubectl exec including background jobs, orphan processes, pid 1 adoption, and waiting behavior belong to area cli, regardless of mentioning kubectl, container runtime, kubelet, node, or generic API terms.

Requests for new API fields/labels/permissions or new handling for edge/race/recreate cases are feature, but concrete failures of existing functionality such as scheduler binding not waking unschedulable pods or OpenAPI verifier failing on typed List resources are bug, not feature.

Reports mentioning CoreDNS/coredns/DNS timeout logs without reproduction steps are support in area apps, not network; only ineffective RBAC resourceName restriction enforcement belongs to area api-machinery, while missing existence validation for roleRef, roles, bindings or service accounts belongs to area auth as bug.

Reports describing secrets encryption, OIDC/OAuth settings, webhook authz request contents such as missing group info, node authorizer graph update delays/caching, or other auth configuration as not working, discarded, ignored, delayed, or otherwise fails without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support, not bug.
Reports describing a CVE, security vulnerability, path traversal, or authentication bypass are kind bug, not support, even without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace.

If PVC, PV, emptyDir, or volume terms co-occur with pod/kubelet/node terms choose area storage over node, and if kubectl auth, can-i, or RBAC verb terms co-occur with kubectl choose area auth over cli.

If EgressSelectorConfiguration, API-server egress/control-plane traffic, or TLS Server Name override terms appear choose area api-machinery or auth over network, and if high I/O, disk pressure, or disk/volume I/O terms appear with node NotReady or kubelet pressure choose area storage over node.

Issues about Deployments/desired-state placement including onto master/control-plane nodes, or about pod status/phase reporting such as OutOfCpu/Completed/Init, belong to area apps (or node if kubelet execution is named), not scheduling.
If the title starts with KEP- then kind is feature, and if the title or body names a specific failed test or Test Report with observed failure output then kind is bug, not support.

PSP and empty-PSP handling belong to area auth, while RBAC enforcement for nonResourceURLs such as /healthz and pod-update Forbidden field-immutability errors belong to area api-machinery; a named RBAC rule plus URL not working counts as defect evidence for bug, while Forbidden update errors without reproduction steps, logs, or stack trace are support.
